extracted.intended_audience: NIH/NIAID grant applicants and peer reviewers (R21-level biomedical investigators)
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of the review criteria and evaluative guidance used in an NIAID/CSR summary statement for an R21 application, showing the formal NIH review dimensions (Significance, Investigator(s), Innovation, Approach, Environment) plus related administrative and protection criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact / Impact/Priority Score
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall Impact: (panel summary of the application's likely impact and enthusiasm; an overall impact/priority score was assigned).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel commentary summarizes enthusiasm/concerns and then an overall impact/priority score is calculated after discussion. Note on scoring: 'The impact/priority score is calculated after discussion of an application by averaging the overall scores (1-9) given by all voting reviewers on the committee and multiplying by 10.' Criterion scores are submitted prior to the meeting, are not discussed specifically at the review meeting, and are not calculated into the overall impact score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates whether the project addresses an important problem or a critical barrier to progress in the field. (Score examples shown: 1-4 in critiques.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengths noted: importance of Legionella as pathogen/model; addressing redundancy of ~150 effectors; potential temporal assessment of host response; long-term goal to target host proteins as 'host-based' antibiotics. Weaknesses/concerns: main concern that protein stability may not reflect effector action and thus limit utility; redundancy of effectors may remain a concern; screen may not resolve effectors that yield post-translational modifications rather than altering stability (though downstream stability effects are possible). Consideration: whether the assay's resolution is sufficient to capture biologically relevant changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses the qualifications, productivity, and suitability of the PD/PI(s), collaborators, and other researchers to accomplish the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengths: experienced investigator with strong publication record and relevant expertise in bacterial pathogenesis and immunology. Weaknesses: investigator has not published extensively on Legionella (though some relevant experience exists). Review notes evaluate whether the team has appropriate track record and experience for the specific organism/approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Considers whether the application challenges current research paradigms or uses novel concepts, approaches, or methodologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengths: highly innovative adaptation of the Global Protein Stability (GPS) system to bacterial pathogenesis; novel approach to study host protein stability at scale. Weaknesses: uncertainty that many Legionella effectors will elicit measurable protein stability changes; concern that some targets may not be detectable by this stability-based screen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates the overall strategy, methodology, analyses, and whether the proposed approach is feasible and appropriately addresses potential problems and alternative strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengths: GPS system appears well-designed for stability analysis; preliminary data support feasibility; clear validation strategies for 'hits' and use of expression library of effectors. Weaknesses/risks: approach limited to effectors that modify stability; difficult to deconvolute effects when multiple effectors act in concert; changes may involve cascades that are hard to parse; may be complicated to modulate expression levels of array components to yield detectable phenotypes; last aim (identifying individual effectors) may be overly ambitious for the R21 timeframe. Operational concerns: lacking letter of agreement from a collaborator providing the effector library (Craig Roy) was noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses whether the scientific environment and institutional support will contribute to success of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengths: outstanding collaborators, excellent research environment, potential access to Elledge libraries and advice, possibility to generate whole-genome GFP-ORF reporters. Weaknesses: missing letter from a specific Legionella biologist (Craig Roy). Quarterly collaborator interactions and institutional support are weighed positively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Health Relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Statement of the relevance of the proposed research to public health (how it may impact disease prevention/treatment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This application proposes identifying host proteins altered by Legionella effectors; understanding these interactions may enable development of new classes of antibiotics or host-targeted therapies. Reviewers considered potential translational impact when assessing significance/impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether human subjects protections apply and are adequate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not Applicable (No Human Subjects). Listed explicitly as a review item to confirm applicability or protections when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether work involves vertebrate animals and, if so, whether protections and justifications are adequate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not Applicable (No live vertebrate animals involved for competing application) — included as a required review item when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of whether proposed work involves biohazards and whether appropriate protections and approvals are in place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not Applicable in some critiques, and listed as 'Acceptable' in another critique. Reviewers explicitly note biohazard status and assess acceptability as part of review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and Safety Monitoring Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement to include a data and safety monitoring plan when applicable (clinical trials).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not Applicable (No Clinical Trials). Reviewers note applicability; when clinical trials are involved, an appropriate plan is required and will be reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of plans to share resources (data, model organisms, reagents) as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as 'Not Applicable (No Relevant Resources)' in this summary. When relevant, resource sharing plans are reviewed and can affect funding decisions or conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support / Committee Budget Recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers/committee may provide recommendations about the requested budget and period of support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative budget note: the budget shown is the requested budget and not yet adjusted; if an award is planned, Institutes will calculate costs based on committee recommendations. In this case 'Recommend as Requested' and 'Budget was recommended as requested' appears. Reviewers may identify recommended budget modifications or possible overlaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications from Foreign Organizations / Select Agents / Other Administrative Compliance Items
rubrics_metrics.description: Checklist items for administrative compliance (foreign organizations, select agents, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this application these items were listed as 'Not Applicable.' The summary statement lists these administrative compliance categories explicitly and indicates applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility / Timeline Fit for Mechanism (R21 appropriateness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment whether the scope and ambition of proposed aims fit the purpose and time/resources of the award mechanism (here, an R21 exploratory/developmental grant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel concern that the application may be overly ambitious for the time and resources of an R21; reviewers suggested using some aims (e.g., screen of E3 ligases) as feasibility experiments to define system parameters. Fit to mechanism (exploratory goals) was considered when assigning impact and approach scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of Support and Collaborator Commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of formal collaborator support (letters of collaboration/agreements) and access to reagents/services promised in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absence of a letter of agreement from a collaborator expected to provide effector library (Craig Roy) was noted as a weakness. Conversely, letter of support from Stephen Elledge indicating advice and library access was seen as a strength. Reviewers weigh documented commitments.
